I don't see these in the patch tree?  Until at least one of those exists, this is just over complicated code.
Modified the commit message
Not sure what this is accomplishing at this point.  Please make sure the usage is aparent in the code you write.  hypotehtical use cases will be be a justification for complexity.
*will not be a justification for complexity.

Our security policy requires that all BMC-to-BMC communication use mTLS channels backed by TPM-based certificates, whereas external communication should continue to use the current default certificates. This is not a general-use requirement and may not be needed by all users. Therefore, bmcweb should be capable of supporting extensions or hooks to allow SSL context creation to be customized for such platform-specific requirements.I can raise a separate commit to demonstrate how this hook would be used in practice.

> Our security policy requires that all BMC-to-BMC communication

This patch has nothing to do with bmc->bmc communication.  Please make sure that you're working with the other people doing this same thing from your company.

> use mTLS channels backed by TPM-based certificates, whereas external communication should continue to use the current default certificates. This is not a general-use requirement and may not be needed by all users. Therefore, bmcweb should be capable of supporting extensions or hooks to allow SSL context creation to be customized for such platform-specific requirements.


The idea of using mtls within a board is not unique to IBM, nor does it justify complexity.  Again, your code that you pushed doesn't do the above, so lets keep this review to what this patch does.

>I can raise a separate commit to demonstrate how this hook would be used in practice.

Please show a patch with a real use case that can merge.  If you can't do that, then this is complexity that you likely will want to maintain in a branch.

Please also keep in touch with the other people trying to solve this problem.
@ed@tanous.net you can see the usage of the concrete factory implementation here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87711 . Yes we are working together to upstream for this feature.
Per cpp core guidelines, do not use new or delete.

plese see the above discussion and references

I’m not sure I fully understand this. What exactly do you mean by ‘if (do other SNI)’, and how is bmcweb expected to be informed about this ‘do other SNI’ behaviour? I’m open to an alternative approach as well, as long as it achieves the same outcome as https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87711.

A normal branch.

>  how is bmcweb expected to be informed about this ‘do other SNI’ behaviour? 

This was exactly my question on the other patch, but putting this in code versus a factory function doesn't change the condition on which we generate the different cert.

Branching based on what condition? 

This factory is invoked whenever a new SSL context needs to be created—for example, when a client installs new server certificates, or in our case, when new satellite BMCs are identified and SPM attestation is completed.The SSL context creation logic can vary significantly depending on factors such as where the certificates reside (e.g., TPM vs. file storage) and the type of connection (mandatory mTLS for internal aggregation vs. standard TLS for external clients).Given this variability, wouldn’t it be better to externalize the SSL context creation logic rather than introducing branches to handle all possible combinations?
